Two men are sitting indoors having a conversation; one man in a gray sweater with a red and yellow pin is answering questions from the other man in a blue sweatshirt who is holding a RODE microphone. The man in the gray sweater opens his eyes wide and gestures with his hands as he exaggerates what he believes the Daily Mail will say about the Labour party leader, Jeremy Corbin. Both men are smiling and relaxed. Two newspaper covers, “The Sun” and “Daily Mail”, appear next to the speaker for the short time he mentions those names. The headline on the “Sun” cover reads, “Don’t Chuck Britain in the COR-BIN,” and below that in smaller print is “Actual Headline,” a play on words, implying a garbage bin, and using the Labour party leader’s name as a pun. On the “Daily Mail” cover, the text reads, “Your tactical voting guide to boost the Tories and Brexit… Let’s Reignite British Spirit.” Both images highlight the satirical nature of the interview and are commentary on those publications’ biases. In the background, other people are sitting at tables, and the warm lighting, wood paneled walls, mirror, bookcase, and lamps give the setting the feeling of a cozy pub.
